tldr: This thread is a reading list of LLM research grouped by shared wording, not one event. From Oct 30 it ran through pruning, Anthropic's Nov 2 provable-inference update, knowledge editing and eval-validity work to Nov 13-16 papers on when a model should abstain, ask or escalate.
whats_new: Nov 18: a contrastive-prototype method detects jailbreak prompts without training a separate guard model, after Nov 16-17 papers on calibrated abstention thresholds and provenance-aware decoding for omnimodal hallucinations.
why_it_matters: Most items are single unreplicated preprints, but the recent run converges on guardrail design: calibrated refusal, modality-aware hallucination control and lightweight jailbreak screening, each a component a serving stack can test.

beats.headline: Efficiency work: extreme-sparsity pruning and an early-stopping audit for reasoning models
beats.summary: Opens the window; a text-to-SQL architecture survey lands the same day.

beats.headline: Anthropic reports progress on zkSNARK-based provable inference
beats.summary: The thread's only lab-published item: cryptographic proofs applied to LLM inference.

beats.headline: Updating what models know: answerability drift, multimodal unlearning and lifelong knowledge editing
beats.summary: Also here: an LLM choosing federated aggregation rules without training.

beats.headline: Judgment under scrutiny: rising rater standards on Chatbot Arena, framing effects and personality benchmarks
beats.summary: These days also bring an LLM AutoML searcher, physics-guided fault diagnosis, a training-simulation benchmark and a cognitive account of learning by thinking.

beats.headline: What do scores measure? ShadowBench and a corrupted-input study probe shortcuts behind passing evals
beats.summary: One tests recall without explicit entity names; the other asks whether LLMs pass NLI on noun-stripped or shuffled inputs.

beats.headline: Knowing when not to answer: black-box uncertainty and an interactive ambiguity-resolution eval
beats.summary: One splits prompt ambiguity from knowledge gaps via API calls only; the other scores when a model should ask versus assume. A tabular anomaly-detection paper lands the same day.

beats.headline: Applied decisions: budgeted malware triage, annotation benchmarking, agent RL environments and an AI-infrastructure survey
beats.summary: The run moves from model internals to LLMs making operational calls under cost and documentation constraints.

beats.headline: Guardrails at the output: calibrated abstention, provenance-aware decoding and jailbreak detection
beats.summary: Nov 16-18 papers each target a control point between the model and the user: when to refuse, which modality to trust, which prompt to block.

open_questions: Does the contrastive-prototype jailbreak detector report false-positive rates on benign prompts and hold up against adaptive attacks?
Does stability-compensated threshold calibration keep its error guarantee when the deployed model or prompt distribution shifts?
Does PACD report the decoding latency or extra forward passes it adds per token?
Does TRIAGE-CPG report which models escalate too rarely or too often under a fixed analysis budget?
Do published unlearning or knowledge-editing methods still pass when probed without explicit entity names, as ShadowBench suggests they may not?
Does Anthropic publish proving cost or latency figures for zkSNARK-based provable inference?
take_for_builders: Before swapping in any of these guardrails, replay your own traffic: measure the jailbreak detector's false-block rate on benign prompts, check that a calibrated abstention threshold holds its error rate on your data, and count the extra model calls each method adds.
